files.purpose: Stylesheet for the marketing site's changelog page. Header comment states it is a faithful port of Droppy's inline changelog <style> block from getdroppy.app/changelog.html, re-tokened for this site's dark palette: geometry, spacing, type sizes and animations are Droppy's, only colours are mapped (light card fills to the dark wells, ink text to the dark text tokens, invisible borders and shadows to this site's flat tokens). It styles the changelog hero, the loading/error/empty state card, the two-column sticky release entries, the animated stable channel pill, the floating glass app icon that glides between entries, grouped change lists, a thanks list, and a 'more' toggle button.
calls_into: site.css class .hero__kicker-mark, overridden here with filter: none
site.css .container, given position: relative and z-index: 1 inside the changelog hero and section
--face-scale custom property, read with fallback 1 but set by the page script that drives .clog-float-icon
state_owned: CSS custom property defaults on :root for the channel pill identity (--channel-deep, --channel-bright, --channel-mid, --channel-glow, --channel-glyph), re-declared identically on .changelog-entry__channel--stable

--font-display redefined on :root as "Inter Tight", "Instrument Sans", "Inter", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif, which overrides site.css's --font-display (that one starts with "Instrument Sans")
--face-scale is consumed with fallback 1 but never declared in this file
side_effects: No JavaScript, no network, no storage; purely presentational

Five infinite CSS animations keep the compositor busy: changelog-spin 0.8s linear, channel-breathe-a 5.4s ease-in-out, channel-breathe-b 7.1s ease-in-out, stable-drizzle-a 4.2s linear, stable-drizzle-b 5.4s linear
platform_assumptions: Assumes a browser with position: sticky, CSS grid, clamp(), custom properties, text-wrap: balance and the :is() selector
The version string's font stack is ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace: SF Mono and Menlo are macOS faces, with Consolas already present as the Windows fallback
No macOS or AppKit API dependence; this is web CSS for the marketing site, not the shipped app
ui_elements: .changelog-hero: padding-top clamp(120px, 18vw, 168px); padding-bottom clamp(20px, 3vw, 40px); position relative
.changelog-hero__inner: max-width 640px; margin-inline auto

.changelog-section: padding-top clamp(40px, 6vw, 80px); padding-bottom clamp(64px, 10vw, 120px); comment says the hero hands off with the shared 120px (40 + 80) and the list ends on the shared last-section 120px before the footer
.changelog-list: flex column, gap clamp(28px, 4vw, 48px), margin-inline auto, max-width 1040px
.changelog-state: flex column centered, gap 16px, padding clamp(48px, 8vw, 96px) 28px, border-radius var(--radius-3xl), background var(--bg-well), border 1px solid var(--border-subtle)
.changelog-state__title: font-size var(--text-base), font-weight 600, color var(--text-primary)
.changelog-state__text: font-size var(--text-sm), color var(--text-tertiary), line-height 1.6, max-width 420px

.changelog-spinner: 28x28px circle, border 2.5px solid var(--bg-well-raised) with border-top-color var(--accent), animation changelog-spin 0.8s linear infinite; under prefers-reduced-motion the animation-duration becomes 2.4s, so it keeps spinning, just slower

.changelog-entry: grid-template-columns minmax(0, 5fr) minmax(0, 7fr), gap clamp(28px, 6vw, 88px), padding-top clamp(40px, 6vw, 72px), border-top 1px solid var(--border-subtle); :first-child gets padding-top 0 and border-top 0
.changelog-entry__pin: position sticky, top 108px
.changelog-entry__date: inline-flex, align-items center, flex-wrap wrap, gap 12px, row-gap 8px, font-size var(--text-sm), color var(--text-tertiary)
.changelog-entry__date::before: 12x12px circle, background var(--accent), box-shadow 0 0 0 4px var(--accent-soft), flex-shrink 0
.changelog-entry.is-stable .changelog-entry__date::before: background #1e40af, box-shadow 0 0 0 4px rgba(30, 64, 175, 0.18)

.changelog-entry__channel pill: inline-flex, gap 5px, padding 4px 11px 4px 9px, border-radius var(--radius-full), background linear-gradient(135deg, var(--channel-deep) 0%, var(--channel-bright) 52%, var(--channel-mid) 100%), color #ffffff, font-size var(--text-xs), font-weight 600, line-height 1.25 pinned on purpose, letter-spacing 0.01em, white-space nowrap, box-shadow 0 1px 8px var(--channel-glow)
.changelog-entry__channel-glyph: 11x11px block, flex-shrink 0, color var(--channel-glyph); comment calls it a droplet on the same 11px silhouette slot Droppy's moon and flask use
.changelog-entry__channel::before and ::after: absolute inset 0, border-radius inherit, pointer-events none, background-repeat no-repeat

.changelog-entry__title: margin-top 18px, font-family var(--font-display), font-size clamp(26px, 3vw, 38px), font-weight 700, letter-spacing -0.03em, line-height 1.08, color var(--text-primary), text-wrap balance
.changelog-entry__version: margin-top 9px, monospace stack, font-size var(--text-xs), letter-spacing 0.01em, color var(--text-quaternary)
.changelog-entry__islot: 84x84px reserved parking spot, margin-top 22px
.clog-float-icon: 84x84px block, pointer-events none, opacity 0, transition opacity 600ms ease, will-change transform; .is-on sets opacity 1

.clog-float-icon__face: absolute inset 0, 84x84px, object-fit contain, opacity 0, transform scale(0.72) rotate(-8deg), filter blur(7px), transition opacity 520ms ease, transform 640ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1), filter 520ms ease
.clog-float-icon__face.is-front: opacity 1, transform scale(var(--face-scale, 1)), filter none
.changelog-entry__summary: font-size var(--text-base), color var(--text-secondary), line-height 1.65

.changelog-group: margin-top 18px; .changelog-group__icon 15x15px, opacity 0.92, flex-shrink 0; .changelog-group__label flex row, gap 7px, font-size var(--text-sm), font-weight 600, color var(--text-primary), margin-bottom 8px

.changelog-thanks: margin-top 18px; .changelog-thanks__label font-size var(--text-sm), weight 600, margin-bottom 8px; .changelog-thanks-list list-style none, padding 0, margin 0, flex column, gap 7px; .changelog-thanks-item font-size var(--text-sm), color var(--text-secondary), line-height 1.55; .changelog-thanks__handle color var(--accent-text), text-decoration none, underline on hover
.changelog-item-list: flex column, gap 7px; .changelog-item position relative, padding-left 18px, font-size var(--text-sm), color var(--text-secondary), line-height 1.55
.changelog-item::before bullet: absolute left 2px, top 0.6em, 4x4px circle, background var(--text-quaternary)

.changelog-more button: margin-top 12px, padding 0, border 0, background none, font inherit then font-size var(--text-sm), font-weight 500, color var(--text-tertiary), cursor pointer, transition color var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out); hover colour var(--text-primary)
@media (max-width: 720px): .changelog-entry becomes grid-template-columns 1fr with gap 20px, and .changelog-entry__pin becomes position static

.scrub-frost: four stacked halos in text-shadow, 0 0 0.05em rgba(11, 14, 20, 0.98), 0 0 0.16em rgba(11, 14, 20, 0.94), 0 0 0.4em rgba(11, 14, 20, 0.88), 0 0 0.85em rgba(11, 14, 20, 0.72); descendants matching :is(a[class*="btn"], button, .btn, .e2ee, .board-tools) get text-shadow: none
feature_notes: The header comment lists everything deliberately DROPPED from Droppy's original changelog styles because there is nothing to wear them on this page: the frame-sequence hero (.changelog-scrub), the light-paper hero ink override, the nightly/beta/iOS/playground/droppykit channel variants and the .is-nightly/.is-beta/.is-ios rules, the channel note, entry actions, TestFlight, galleries, video, image, lightbox, whatsnew label, and the per-platform float-icon faces. Only the stable channel ships.

Release entries are a two-column grid: the left column (date plus display title) pins with position: sticky at top 108px while the right column's notes scroll past, 'like a product-blog changelog' per the comment.

Stable pill animation: two absolutely positioned overlay layers that only ever change opacity, running on two different periods (5.4s and 7.1s) 'so the pill breathes unevenly rather than pulsing in unison'. channel-breathe-a goes 0.55 at 0%/100% and 1 at 50%; channel-breathe-b goes 1 at 0%/100% and 0.5 at 50%.

Stable droplet streams: ::before background-image is radial-gradient(circle at 7px 4px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.90) 0 0.8px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 2px) plus radial-gradient(circle at 14px 13px, rgba(219, 231, 255, 0.75) 0 0.6px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 1.6px), background-size 20px 20px, animation stable-drizzle-a 4.2s linear infinite. ::after is radial-gradient(circle at 4px 12px, rgba(219, 231, 255, 0.80) 0 0.7px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 1.8px) plus radial-gradient(circle at 16px 5px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.70) 0 1px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 2.3px), background-size 24px 24px, background-position 8px 0, animation stable-drizzle-b 5.4s linear infinite.

Seamlessness rule: each drizzle keyframe scrolls its repeating tile by exactly one tile height downward, in px so a seam is impossible at any rounding. stable-drizzle-a goes from background-position 0 -20px to 0 0; stable-drizzle-b goes from 8px -24px to 8px 0. Comment: 'the loop is seamless and no droplet ever pops or respawns'.

prefers-reduced-motion: reduce kills both pill overlay animations and pins them at opacity 0.9, and flattens .clog-float-icon__face to scale(var(--face-scale, 1)) with filter none and a 320ms opacity-only transition, keeping the dissolve and dropping the movement.
The marker dot takes its channel's colour, #1e40af for stable, 'so the row reads as one thing'.

Comment on .changelog-entry__version: the headline above is the human name for the release, the version is the exact build string kept for support and bug reports, 'the thing you paste into a post', so it stays literal and stays quiet.
Comment: stable is royal blue on purpose because it is the tier the download button gives you.

The single .clog-float-icon carries only one face, the Droppy Code artwork; it cross-dissolves with a little scale and blur on hand-off between entries so the icon reads as gliding down the page rather than being swapped.

The comment for .scrub-frost says Droppy's halo is paper-coloured for its light art, while here it is canvas-coloured (rgba(11, 14, 20, ...) matches --bg-top #0b0e14) for the dark page, and one class on the copy group covers kicker, title and subtitle at once.
unresolved_questions: The markup that pairs with these classes lives in website/changelog.html, which is not in this bundle, so the exact user-visible strings for .changelog-state__title, .changelog-state__text and the .changelog-more toggle label cannot be determined from this file.
--face-scale is consumed with fallback 1 but never declared here; the script that positions .clog-float-icon must set it per face, and that script is not in this bundle.

.changelog-entry.is-stable is the only channel state class kept, but whether the page script can still emit other is-* channel classes (which would then fall through to the :root defaults) cannot be established from CSS alone.

.scrub-frost's exclusion selector references .e2ee and .board-tools; neither class is defined in this file or in site.css, so they look like leftovers from the upstream Droppy page, but that cannot be confirmed from this bundle.
.changelog-hero .hero__kicker-mark sets filter: none to undo a recolor, but the original filter is not in this file (it lived in Droppy's inline block), so what it undid is not recoverable here.

files.purpose: The single shared design system stylesheet for the whole Droppy Code marketing site. Header comment: 'A dark port of the getdroppy.app design system: the same notch dock, pills, reveal motion, highlight rail, FAQ and footer, re-tokened for a deep code-editor canvas and the blue of the Droppy Code icon. The binary field and the tile system are new and live at the bottom.' It declares every design token, the reset, the site-wide anti-copy lockdown, the fixed notch nav with its spring-open intro, the button morph-hover system, the hero with its animated charged word and binary canvas field, feature cards, the horizontal highlight rail, the tile card system, agent marks, usage limits, stats, the free and open-source card that takes the pricing slot, the zig-zag FAQ accordion, the outro, the footer with its giant wordmark, and the theme picker plus binary twinkles. Explicitly no build step, one stylesheet, one page.
key_symbols: :root token block (colors, radii, fonts, type scale, container, nav geometry, easings, durations)

Reset: *, *::before, *::after; html; body (declared twice, second rule adds the anti-copy lockdown); img, video (twice); a; button; h1,h2,h3,h4,p; ul,ol; code,kbd,pre; ::selection; :where(a,button,input,select,textarea,[tabindex]):focus-visible; .nav :focus-visible
second :root block with --nav-dock-* tokens; @keyframes navDockExpand; html.nav-intro-done .nav__pill
calls_into: changelog.css consumes this file's tokens (--bg-well, --bg-well-raised, --radius-3xl, --radius-full, --accent, --accent-soft, --accent-text, --text-*, --dur-fast, --ease-out) and overrides --font-display and .hero__kicker-mark

site.js builds the two .btn-morph__face layers at runtime 'so button markup stays plain', and toggles .is-tapmorph, .is-open (nav pill and FAQ item), .is-visible and .is-settled (reveal), .is-dragging (highlight rail), .is-current (theme stage image and name), .is-active (nav link)
A head-inline gate script adds html.nav-intro-done on later loads so the nav dock intro never replays between pages
Canvas elements inside .hero__field and .outro__field, driven by the binary-field script
Fonts Inter (body/UI), Instrument Sans and Inter Tight (display), loaded in the page head per the header comment
state_owned: Canvas tokens: --bg-top #0b0e14, --bg-bottom #0b0e14, --bg-well #131823, --bg-well-raised #1a2030; color-scheme: dark
Solid dark tokens: --ink #05070b, --notch-ink var(--ink), --surface-dark var(--ink), --text-on-dark #e6ebf3, --text-on-dark-soft rgba(230, 235, 243, 0.68)

Glass tokens: --glass-bg rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05), --glass-bg-strong rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08), --glass-border transparent, --glass-border-strong transparent, --glass-blur blur(20px) saturate(180%), --glass-blur-soft blur(14px) saturate(150%)

Text tokens: --text-primary #e8edf5, --text-secondary rgba(232, 237, 245, 0.72), --text-tertiary rgba(232, 237, 245, 0.55), --text-quaternary rgba(232, 237, 245, 0.38)
Status tokens: --color-success #3fd08a, --color-error #ff6b6b, --color-warning #fbbf24
Intentionally invisible: --border-subtle transparent, --border-strong transparent, --shadow-card none

Type scale: --text-xs 0.75rem, --text-sm 0.875rem, --text-base 1rem, --text-lg 1.125rem, --text-xl 1.25rem, --text-2xl 1.5rem, --text-3xl 1.875rem, --text-4xl 2.25rem, --text-5xl 3rem, --text-6xl 3.75rem
Layout: --container-width 1120px, --container-pad 24px (18px under 480px), --gap-heading 48px described as 'the one distance between a section's heading block and what follows it'

Nav geometry: --nav-safe-top env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px), --nav-dock-bar-height 8px, --nav-dock-closed-height 56px (54px under 720px), --site-hero-nav-gap 104px (58px under 720px), --site-hero-content-start calc(var(--nav-safe-top) + var(--nav-dock-bar-height) + var(--nav-dock-closed-height) + var(--site-hero-nav-gap))
Motion: --ease-out cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), --ease-out-soft cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), --dur-fast 150ms, --dur-base 300ms, --dur-slow 600ms

Nav dock intro tokens in a second :root block: --nav-dock-duration 640ms, --nav-dock-curve cubic-bezier(0.32, 1.22, 0.36, 1), --nav-dock-intro-delay 120ms, --nav-dock-collapsed-transform translateY(-6px) scaleX(0.78), --nav-dock-collapsed-blur blur(8px), --nav-dock-fade-duration calc(var(--nav-dock-duration) * 0.55), --nav-dock-exit-curve cubic-bezier(0.32, 1, 0.36, 1)

Component-local properties: --notch-bar; --notch-fillet 24px; --notch-fillet-inset 0px (becomes var(--notch-fillet) under the border-shape @supports); --pill-pad-right 7px (10px under 720px); --pill-pad-left 12px (14px under 720px, 12px under 380px)

Morph properties: --morph-dur 340ms, --morph-ease cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), --morph-blur 16px (11px on .footer__cta, .btn--sm and .nav__cta), --morph-tap-dur 620ms, --morph-mark-size default 20px, 26px on .btn--applepill and .btn--darkpill, 17px on footer/sm/nav CTAs
Rail properties: --highlight-card-width min(820px, calc(100vw - 48px)); --highlight-page-gutter max(24px, calc((100vw - 1240px) / 2 + 24px))
--reveal-delay, read with fallback 0ms on .reveal but never set here
side_effects: No JavaScript in this file. It does declare animations that run forever: hero-charge-sheen 3.2s linear infinite and bit-twinkle 4.5s ease-in-out infinite across 12 staggered spans

body background-image embeds an inline data:image/svg+xml grain texture, width 160 height 160, filter id='n' with feTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.85' numOctaves='2' stitchTiles='stitch' and feColorMatrix tinting to 0.75 / 0.82 / 0.95 at alpha 0.035, background-repeat repeat. Comment: 'The same whisper of grain as the Droppy site, inverted for the dark canvas so it lifts rather than dirties.'

.hero__charged-sheen embeds a second inline data:image/svg+xml, width 240 height 64 viewBox 0 0 240 64, four copies of the bolt path 'M12 2 4 30h9l-3 22 12-30h-9z' filled %23ffffff at fill-opacity .6, translated to (20 4), (80 4), (140 4), (200 4), each with scale(1.1)
Selection, drag and long-press are suppressed site-wide; the comment says the scripts back this up by swallowing copy, cut, drag and the context menu
platform_assumptions: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) drives --nav-safe-top: an iOS/iPadOS Safari safe-area concept used to push the fixed nav below a device notch

--font-mono is ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace, an Apple-only stack with no Windows fallback; the header comment says 'Code inside the chips uses the Mac's own SF Mono; nothing else is imported', so on Windows the generic monospace would be used
-webkit-backdrop-filter paired with backdrop-filter on .glass and .btn--darkpill targets WebKit/Safari first
-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%, -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased and -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale; the grayscale smoothing hint is macOS-specific
-webkit-touch-callout: none, -webkit-user-drag: none and -webkit-user-select: none are Safari/iOS specifics used for the anti-copy lockdown
-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch on .showcase-highlights__rail is an iOS Safari momentum-scroll hint, alongside a ::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none } rule
border-shape: shape(...) sits behind @supports as progressive enhancement over the two radial-gradient fillet pseudo-elements; it is a very new CSS feature likely only in Safari at the pinned commit
min-height: 100dvh, aspect-ratio, overflow-x: clip, text-wrap: balance / pretty, grid-template-rows 0fr animation and the [inert] attribute selector all require a modern engine
The .hero__apple glyph and the .btn--applepill CTA assume a Mac download is the primary action
ui_elements: .skip-link: fixed at top calc(var(--nav-safe-top) + 12px), left 50%, z-index 101, padding 10px 16px, border-radius var(--radius-md), background var(--text-primary), color var(--ink), font-size var(--text-sm), weight 600; hidden at transform translate(-50%, -160%) and slid to translate(-50%, 0) on :focus-visible with transition var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out)
Global focus ring: outline 3px solid var(--accent) with outline-offset 3px; inside .nav the outline-color becomes #7ab8ff
::selection: background var(--accent-soft-strong), color #fff
.container: max-width var(--container-width), margin-inline auto, padding-inline var(--container-pad); .visually-hidden uses the 1x1 clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0) pattern
section: position relative, padding-block clamp(40px, 6vw, 80px); .section-tight is identical

.section-heading: "Inter Tight" then var(--font-display), weight 600, letter-spacing -0.045em, line-height 1.05, font-size clamp(2.25rem, 5.5vw, 3.25rem), centered, margin-bottom 18px, text-wrap balance
.section-subtitle: font-size clamp(1.05rem, 2.2vw, 1.25rem), color var(--text-tertiary), line-height 1.45, max-width 720px, centered, text-wrap pretty
.surface-well: background var(--bg-well), border-radius var(--radius-3xl)

.reveal: opacity 0 with translateY(24px), transition opacity and transform over var(--dur-slow) var(--ease-out) with transition-delay var(--reveal-delay, 0ms); .is-visible restores opacity 1 and translateY(0); .is-settled sets transform none and transition none; prefers-reduced-motion sets transition-duration 1ms and transform none

.nav: fixed at top var(--nav-safe-top), left/right 0, z-index 100, flex centered, pointer-events none; .nav::before paints a var(--notch-ink) bar at top calc(-1 * var(--nav-safe-top) - 1px) with height calc(var(--nav-safe-top) + var(--notch-bar) + 2px)

.nav__pill: pointer-events auto, flex, gap 10px, width fit-content, height 56px, margin-top var(--notch-bar), padding 6px calc(var(--pill-pad-right) + var(--notch-fillet-inset)) 6px calc(var(--pill-pad-left) + var(--notch-fillet-inset)), border-radius 0 0 var(--radius-xl) var(--radius-xl), background var(--notch-ink), max-width calc(100% - 2 * var(--notch-fillet) + 2 * var(--notch-fillet-inset))

.nav__pill::before/::after fillets: 24px wide, height calc(var(--notch-fillet) + var(--notch-bar)), at top calc(-1 * var(--notch-bar)); ::before is left calc(-1 * fillet + 1px) with radial-gradient(circle var(--notch-fillet) at 0 100%, transparent calc(fillet - 1px), var(--notch-ink) fillet); ::after mirrors it at right with at 100% 100%
.nav__logo: flex gap 8px, var(--font-display), weight 600, font-size var(--text-base), color var(--text-on-dark), margin-right 10px; its img height 24px, width auto, border-radius 6px

.nav__links: flex gap 22px, margin-right 8px; .nav__link font-size var(--text-sm), weight 500, color var(--text-on-dark-soft), white-space nowrap, transition color var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out); :hover and .is-active go to var(--text-on-dark); .nav__links[inert] gets pointer-events none
.btn.nav__cta: border-radius var(--radius-full), background var(--text-primary), color var(--ink); hover background #fff; active background #cdd5e1

.nav__menu hamburger: display none by default, 40x40px, border-radius 12px, transparent background, gap 4px; its three spans are 16x2px with border-radius 2px and background #e8eaed, transition transform 320ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 1.22, 0.36, 1) and opacity 180ms ease; .nav__pill.is-open rotates span 1 to translateY(6px) rotate(45deg), sets span 2 opacity 0, rotates span 3 to translateY(-6px) rotate(-45deg)

@media (max-width: 720px) nav: pill width and max-width calc(100vw - 2 * fillet + 2 * fillet-inset - 8px), height auto with min-height var(--nav-dock-closed-height), flex-wrap wrap, column-gap 10px, row-gap 0; .nav__logo margin-right auto; .nav__menu display inline-flex; .nav__links order 5, flex-basis 100%, column, align-items stretch, gap 2px, max-height 0, opacity 0, overflow hidden, padding 0 4px, transitions max-height 560ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 1.22, 0.36, 1), opacity 240ms ease, padding 560ms same curve; open state sets max-height 360px, opacity 1, padding 10px 4px 8px; .nav__link padding 13px 12px, border-radius 12px, font-size 15px, :active background rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)
@media (max-width: 380px): .nav__pill --pill-pad-left 12px, and .nav__logo span display none so only the mark remains

@keyframes navDockExpand: 0% opacity 0 with var(--nav-dock-collapsed-transform) and filter var(--nav-dock-collapsed-blur); 55% opacity 1; 100% opacity 1, transform translateY(0) scaleX(1), filter blur(0). Applied to .nav__pill with transform-origin 50% 0 and animation-fill-mode both

feature_notes: Site-wide anti-copy lockdown: body gets -webkit-user-select and user-select none plus -webkit-touch-callout none, and img and video get -webkit-user-drag none and pointer-events none. Comment: 'Nothing on the page is for taking: no text selection, no dragging a picture or a film off the page, no long-press sheet on a phone. The scripts back this up by swallowing copy, cut, drag and the context menu.' A follow-up comment notes the theme picker's names are buttons and the FAQ questions are buttons, so those keep their pointer events; only the media itself is inert.
html gets overflow-x: clip, -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100% and scroll-behavior: smooth globally; body gets min-height 100dvh, line-height 1.6 and the grain background.

The nav dock springs open once per visit: the pill runs navDockExpand for 640ms on cubic-bezier(0.32, 1.22, 0.36, 1) after a 120ms delay, starting collapsed at translateY(-6px) scaleX(0.78) with blur(8px), 'like the Droppy shelf (shelf curve + blur snapping into focus)'. A head-inline gate adds html.nav-intro-done on later loads so it never replays when navigating between pages; prefers-reduced-motion also sets animation: none. The comment states the tokens and keyframes are the getdroppy.app ones, unchanged.

The notch fillets are drawn twice: as radial-gradient pseudo-elements by default, and, where the browser supports border-shape: shape(...), as one border-shape path while ::before and ::after get content: none and --notch-fillet-inset becomes var(--notch-fillet) so the padding compensates.

Morph hover is 'the one hover every button on the site shares'. Two stacked content layers (a REST face and a HOVER face) are built at runtime by site.js so button markup stays plain; on hover the label dissolves through a thick gaussian blur where it stands and a fitting glyph blurs in, centred. The comment is emphatic in capitals: 'NOTHING SLIDES AND NOTHING RESIZES: the silhouette is identical at rest and hovered, only the content changes.'

Hover is gated behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) because 'on iOS Safari a synthesised hover would swallow the first tap'; touch gets the same morph from the .is-tapmorph class, which runs the 620ms tap-out and tap-in animations. .btn-morph--icon swaps faces; .btn-morph--label only runs the 340ms dissolve on its rest face.

Under prefers-reduced-motion the morph system removes the hover face entirely (display: none), cancels the label dissolve and both tap animations, keeps the rest face at opacity 1 with filter none, and falls back to .btn-morph:hover { opacity: 0.85 }.

The hero's charged word replays the choreography of 'Supercharged' on getdroppy.app: once the headline's reveal settles (.is-settled) a strike drops into the word from the top of the viewport over 850ms, an arrival bloom pulses once over 900ms, and a sheen keeps sweeping through the letters at 3.2s linear forever. The comment says Droppy's strike is a lightning bolt while here it is a stream of ones and zeros, and the sheen carries a row of digits instead of a bolt, although the embedded sheen SVG still draws four bolt paths.

Before the headline settles, .hero__title:not(.is-settled) hides the sheen, the charge entry and the ::after bloom with display: none; a will-change: opacity, transform compositing hint is held only while the shared reveal runs and is dropped to auto under reduced motion.

The binary field behind the hero is one canvas fixed to the hero's box, masked with linear-gradient(180deg, #000 0%, #000 55%, transparent 100%) 'so it melts into the page before the promo block'. The outro repeats the idea with radial-gradient(60% 70% at 50% 50%, #000 20%, transparent 100%).

Every tour still is a whole 16:10 frame, so .hero__film, .fcard__media, .fcard__media--window, .highlight-card .fcard__media and .wordscroll__demo-video all use aspect-ratio 16 / 10; the comments say a 16:9 or window-shaped box with cover cropped their edges, and .wordscroll__demo-video therefore uses object-fit contain so no bars and no crop.

The highlight rail is a full-bleed (100vw, margin-left calc(50% - 50vw)) horizontally scrolling, mandatory snap-stopped, drag-scrollable carousel with two round arrow buttons that disable at the ends at opacity 0.28 and cursor default; reduced motion turns off smooth scrolling and the arrow transitions.

The tile system is declared as the one card system: 'Every card on the page is a tile: a big-radius well with generous padding, one bold label, and either a large illustration or a visual that is allowed to bleed off the edge. Nothing else lives in a tile: no small icon chips, no key caps, no paragraphs under paragraphs.'

Picture tiles (.tile--fade) keep copy and capture apart: the copy sits at the top and the capture stands under it, running off the bottom and one side and fading out before the edge. Comment: 'Never under the words: the copy keeps its own band, the picture takes what is left.'

The FAQ list reads as a back-and-forth zig-zag: every question is a content-sized pill drawn by a ::before pseudo-element (so the round button can sit outside it on the page canvas and the row still works when a page ships the question as a bare text node), only every second one is pushed right with margin-left auto, and the answer card mirrors to the opposite side with a 28px accent dot in the side margin. Phones take the full-width pill back for both sides and hide the dots.

The FAQ answer opens with the grid-template-rows 0fr to 1fr technique over var(--dur-base) 300ms, and the icon swaps its plus svg (hidden via visibility: hidden, so the circle keeps its size) for a 16x2px minus bar while filling with var(--accent).
The free and open-source card explicitly 'takes the pricing slot' and is centred 'as the pricing card on getdroppy.app is'.

The footer wordmark is a giant clipped word at rgba(232, 237, 245, 0.05) inside a fixed-height overflow-hidden box with will-change: transform and transform translateY(0.06em), implying a script-driven parallax translate.

The theme picker is one big window in the chosen theme plus the names to pick from, and lives inside the second wordscroll's demo slot. Its width is min(1040px, 86vw, calc(60vh * 2080 / 1426)) so that the window, its 26 names and the caption all fit the pinned stage together; the stage is at the same 2080 / 1426 aspect ratio.
The .wordscroll__bits binary twinkles are described as replacing Droppy's sparks.

Comments declare the intentional flat look: --border-subtle and --border-strong are transparent tokens kept only so rules can reference them ('Kept as tokens, intentionally invisible: flat look, no outlines'), and --shadow-card is none ('Disabled: flat look, no shadows, no glow effects').
unresolved_questions: Several classes are styled here but their markup lives in website/*.html and their behavior in website/assets/js/*, none of which are in this bundle: the .wordscroll__* mechanism (only __demo-video and __bits are styled here), the .hero__charge-entry inner SVG content, and the theme picker's 26 theme names.

.tile__rows has only a mobile override (margin 8px -28px 0 0 under 620px) and no base rule anywhere in this file, so its default layout must come from elsewhere or the base rule was dropped in the port.

--nav-dock-fade-duration and --nav-dock-exit-curve are declared in the second :root block but never referenced in this file; they may be consumed by site.js or be dead carry-over from getdroppy.app, and that cannot be decided from CSS alone.

Declared but unused in this file: --radius-2xl, --accent-hover, --accent-active, --accent-glow, --color-error, --color-warning, --surface-dark, --glass-border, --glass-border-strong, --shadow-card, --bg-bottom, --text-3xl, --text-4xl, --text-5xl, --text-6xl. Whether another stylesheet or script reads them is not determinable from this bundle.

.outro__icon-wrap::before is explicitly set to content: none, which suggests it cancels a glow from the upstream Droppy sheet; the original rule is not present here, so the intended appearance it removes cannot be recovered.

The header comment says the fonts are loaded in the page head, so the exact <link> or @font-face declarations are in the HTML, not this file. Notably "Inter Tight" is named first in many rules but is not part of --font-display, so whether it is actually requested cannot be confirmed here.
